The '''2016–17 Bundesliga''' was the 54th season of the [[Bundesliga]], Germany's premier [[Association football|football]] competition. It began on 26 August 2016 and ended on 20 May 2017.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.worldfootball.net/competition/co12/se20812/all-matches/ |title=Bundesliga 2016/2017 » Schedule |website=WorldFootball.net |access-date=13 June 2020}}</ref> [[FC Bayern Munich|Bayern Munich]] were the defending champions. Fixtures for the 2016–17 season were announced on 29 June 2016.<ref>{{cite news|title=The new 2016/2017 Bundesliga and Bundesliga 2 schedule|publisher= bundesliga.com |url= http://schedule.bundesliga.com/|date=23 June 2016|access-date=23 June 2016}}</ref>

[[Bayern Munich]] won their 26th Bundesliga title with three games to spare, becoming the first team to win 5 consecutive titles.<ref>{{cite web|url= http://www.espn.co.uk/football/report?gameId=456618|title= Bayern Munich seal Bundesliga crown for record fifth straight year|date=1 May 2017|work=ESPN|access-date=3 May 2017}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url= https://www.theguardian.com/football/2017/apr/29/bayern-munich-win-bundesliga-title-wolfsburg-match-report|title= Bayern Munich seal fifth consecutive Bundesliga title with Wolfsburg win|date=1 May 2017|work=Guardian|access-date=3 May 2017}}</ref> [[RB Leipzig]] became the runners-up, only a year after its promotion last season from the [[2015–16 2. Bundesliga]].

==Teams==
A total of 18 teams participated in this edition of the Bundesliga. [[VfB Stuttgart]] and [[Hannover 96]] were relegated to [[2016–17 2. Bundesliga]]. Former Bundesliga champion Stuttgart were relegated to the second level after 39 years, whereas Hannover 96 finished a 14-year stint in the top level. They were replaced by 2. Bundesliga champion [[SC Freiburg]] and 2. Bundesliga runner-up [[RB Leipzig]]. Freiburg immediately returned to the Bundesliga, whereas RB Leipzig made its debut. Finally [[Eintracht Frankfurt]], 16th of Bundesliga faced [[1. FC Nürnberg]], third of 2. Bundesliga in a Bundesliga play-off. Eintracht won 2–1 on aggregate and remained in the top level.

RB Leipzig was the first team from the former [[East Germany]] to play in the Bundesliga since the relegation of [[FC Energie Cottbus|Energie Cottbus]] after the [[2008–09 Bundesliga|2008–09 season]].
